newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sugar prices rise after formal cane edict.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sugar prices rise after formal cane edict.

text.p: Mexican domestic sugar prices have risen in recent trading days in what is seen as a knee-jerk reaction to the government publishing the formal formula that work out cane prices, sources said Monday.

According to market sources and reports, retail sugar prices have risen to 6.3 pesos per kilo from 5 pesos while wholesale prices have inched up around 5 percent on the higher demand from supermarkets and stores.
Sugar prices are no longer controlled in Mexico and are at the whim of supply and demand.

Last week, Mexico's government formally published through its Official Gazette the annual formula for working out cane prices, a pythagoras-like system basically based on international market prices and cane yields.
The formula, which gave an average 26 percent hike to cane growers, was agreed back in January and avoided a national cane growers strike at the start of the traditional November-June crop cycle.

Cane growers annually go into talks with mill owners to thrash out a cane price deal, always threatening a down-machetes strike that is basically a refusal to hand over cane for industrialists to mill.

"There is higher demand on from retailers and that is what is pushing the wholesale price higher," said one sugar trader in Mexico City's massive wholesale market known as the Central de Abastos. He said 50 kg bag prices were oscilating around 200 pesos Monday from an average of 190 last month.
The National Sugar Chamber told Reforma newspaper that it expected to offset the higher cane prices paid to growers by higher sugar wholesale prices of around 10 percent.

The chamber told Reforma that unrefined sugar prices were 186 pesos "some days ago". That, according to the daily, would mean that if the chamber's 10 percent increase panned out, that prices would move up to around 205 pesos per bag. Chamber spokesmen were not immediately for comment.
A spokesman for the National Cane Growers Association said the increase in sugar prices was a knee-jerk move on the part of retailers.

"The cane price has effectively been in operation for two months or we would be on strike right now. The government published the cane price formula and people thought it was new, so started to look to increase prices," he said, asking to remain anonymous.

"If the government wants to avoid confusing situations such as this where traders speculate and raise prices on old news it should be more open and publish its actions in a much more timely manner," he added.

Domestic price increases have little impact on Mexico's sugar end-users. Most, such as major bottlers and confectioners, are vertically integrated into the sugar chain and have stakes in mills or set purchase contracts.
But sugar prices at the retail level do impact Mexico's consumer price index and cause inflation, which was one reason why the government controlled prices of the sweetner up to February 1996.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
